source: OWASP Top 10 cross-walk distilled from owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications, owasp.org/www-project-agentic-security-initiative, OWASP MCP/Skills working drafts (2026), and OWASP ML Top 10 (2024).

categories.summary: Adversarial input overrides the system prompt or coerces an action the user did not intend.

categories.theme: Sensitive data leak from model output
categories.summary: The model emits secrets, training data, or another tenant's content via its output.
A compromised model, fine-tune, dataset, plugin, MCP server, or skill reaches production.
Adversaries plant samples in training, fine-tune, RAG, agent memory, or skill catalog to bias outputs.

categories.theme: Improper output handling at the call site
categories.summary: Caller treats LLM/MCP/skill output as safe HTML, SQL, shell, or eval input → XSS, SQLi, RCE.

categories.owasp_asi: ASI02 Tool Misuse / ASI03 Privilege Compromise
categories.summary: Tools/agents/skills hold more privilege than the calling user actually has.
Adversary acts as another user or system in agent / MCP / skill traffic.
Token amplification, recursive prompts, or expensive tool calls drive cost or denial of service.

categories.owasp_asi: ASI05 Cascading Hallucinations / ASI07 Deceptive Behavior
categories.summary: The model emits confident but wrong output; cascading through agents/tools compounds the harm.

categories.owasp_ml: ML03 Model Inversion / ML04 Membership Inference
categories.summary: Embeddings or model parameters leak training-set membership or reconstruct private inputs.
